problem_statement: mattverse/what-i-love contains a finished Next.js 15 App Router portfolio under `35-portfolio`: the Matt Park Archive, a dark-ink (#16161D) motion casebook with lavender (#D2D2FF) Grad/IBM Plex typography, a hero ("Motion Archive Casebook"), a set of real-time motion and shader experiments backed by local MP4/PNG assets, and a data-driven `/project/[slug]` case-study route (Good Time, Reflective Cube). The archive works across four real mediums — post-processing, 3D materials, interaction, and gradient fields — but a visitor cannot actually browse the pieces by medium: the disciplines live only in scattered section headings and there is no way to narrow the work or carry that index onto the case studies. Build the archive's OWN "Selected experiments" browser: a real filter-by-medium control (tabs All / Post-processing / 3D Materials / Interaction / Gradient, derived from the pieces' own medium metadata) that sits IN the work area below the hero and, when a tab is clicked, actually re-renders the experiment grid to the matching medium and updates a genuine result count (for example "Showing all 18 experiments" becomes "Showing 7 of 18 experiments · Post-processing"). The browser is a shared, continuous index: its tab row, title, and count readout ride the archive home AND the Good Time and Reflective Cube case studies, while the full experiment grid renders on the home page where the work lives. Keep the Matt Park Archive identity — the dark ink ground, quiet #1E1E27 cards, lavender headings, muted #A5A5E0 helper text, Grad/IBM Plex type, the local motion assets, and the hero which must stay first on the page. The filter tab row and the filtered grid must stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal overflow, lay out cleanly (tiles reflow into columns rather than overlapping or clipping), keep the active tab legible (not dark-on-dark), and emit no runtime console or network errors.
required_content: A real "Selected experiments" filter-by-medium control (tabs All / Post-processing / 3D Materials / Interaction / Gradient) sits in the work area below the hero; clicking a medium tab re-renders the experiment grid to the matching medium.

The control shows a genuine result count that re-derives from the active filter (e.g. "Showing all 18 experiments" becomes "Showing 7 of 18 experiments · Post-processing" when the Post-processing tab is selected).

The experiments browser (its tab row, "Selected experiments" title, and count readout) is shared across the archive and appears on the home page AND on the /project/good-time and /project/reflective-cube case studies (cross-page continuity); the full experiment grid renders on the home page.

The filter tab row and the filtered grid stay within the 390px mobile viewport with no horizontal page overflow and lay out cleanly (tiles wrap into columns rather than spilling, overlapping, or clipping).

The browser adopts the Matt Park Archive visual system (dark #16161D ground, quiet #1E1E27 cards, lavender #D2D2FF headings, muted #A5A5E0 helper text, Grad/IBM Plex type) and the active tab is clearly legible (not dark-on-dark) — an on-brand casebook index, not an off-palette or broken control.

The existing hero ("Motion Archive Casebook", which stays first on the page), the local MP4/PNG motion assets, the contact links, and the data-driven Good Time / Reflective Cube case studies remain intact and visually stable.
design_constraints: Place the experiments browser IN the work area below the hero and its intro; do NOT pre-empt or sit above the hero title, and do not paste a separate copy of the grid per page.

Build the medium tabs from the experiments' own medium metadata, and render one shared browser component so a single component covers the home and both case-study routes rather than duplicating markup.

Keep the browser native to the Matt Park Archive language: dark #16161D ground, quiet #1E1E27 cards, lavender #D2D2FF headings, muted #A5A5E0 helper text, Grad/IBM Plex type, restrained spacing; keep the active tab legible.

The tab row must wrap or shrink and the filtered grid must reflow into columns within the 390px mobile viewport — do not pin the tabs to a fixed desktop width or force the tiles into a fixed-width non-wrapping row that overflows a phone or overlaps.

The result count and the visible experiment set must both re-derive from the live filter every render so they always match the selected tab; do not snapshot the grid or the count once and leave them stale after a tab is clicked.
Do not recolor the browser into an off-brand palette or replace the local MP4/PNG motion assets with external stock media; reuse the archive's own pieces and design tokens.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the archive home with the hero ("Motion Archive Casebook") first; the Selected-experiments browser is present below the hero and intro.
mobile_initial captures the same home at 390px, where the filter tab row and grid must stay within the viewport with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_work_grid scrolls to the Selected-experiments browser and captures the medium-tab row, the count readout, and the full 18-piece experiment grid (All filter) laid out cleanly.
mobile_work_grid scrolls to the Selected-experiments browser at 390px and captures the tab row and grid reflowed within the viewport with no overflow.

desktop_filter_post captures the browser after clicking the Post-processing tab: the grid re-filters to the seven post-processing pieces and the count updates to "Showing 7 of 18 experiments · Post-processing".
desktop_good_time captures the /project/good-time case study; the shared Selected-experiments browser must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
desktop_reflective captures the /project/reflective-cube case study; the shared Selected-experiments browser must also be present here (cross-page continuity).
tablet_good_time and mobile_good_time capture the Good Time case study at tablet and mobile widths as responsive regression anchors with their project-specific content and local video source.
All browser content must be inspectable as React/Next DOM, not flattened into screenshots or hidden offscreen.

change_completion: A shared "Selected experiments" filter-by-medium browser is added in the work area below the hero and appears on the home page plus the Good Time and Reflective Cube case studies.
Clicking a medium tab re-renders the experiment grid to that medium and updates the result count to reflect it (e.g. "Showing 7 of 18 experiments · Post-processing").
The Matt Park Archive identity (hero wordmark, local motion assets, contact links, case studies) remains intact alongside the browser.
design_consistency: The browser uses the dark ink / lavender / quiet-card / Grad-IBM-Plex conventions with a legible active tab and stays subordinate to the archive hierarchy (below the hero).
The shared browser rides the home and both case-study routes continuously (tab row + title + count readout).
The browser reads as a refined casebook index native to the archive rather than an off-palette or broken control.
regression: The hero ("Motion Archive Casebook") stays first on the page and the local MP4/PNG motion assets and contact links still render.
The data-driven /project/[slug] route keeps its project-specific metadata and local video sources on both case studies.
responsive: Desktop lays the medium tabs in a balanced row and the experiment grid in clean auto-fit columns.
Mobile wraps or shrinks the tabs and reflows the grid into columns on a 390px viewport with no horizontal overflow, overlap, or clipping.

author_notes: Repo-grounded Next.js 15 App Router portfolio task at L4 on mattverse/what-i-love (Matt Park Archive), a motion and shader-art casebook. The graded change builds the archive's OWN "Selected experiments" browser: a filter-by-medium control (All / Post-processing / 3D Materials / Interaction / Gradient, built from the pieces' own medium metadata) that actually re-renders the experiment grid and updates a real result count, placed in the work area below the hero and shared across the home and the Good Time and Reflective Cube case studies. It reuses the archive's local MP4/PNG motion assets (good-time.mp4, reflective-cube.mp4, monalisa.mp4, nokia.mp4, and the wider set) and the dark-ink / lavender / quiet-card / Grad-IBM-Plex design language. Four orthogonal machine-checked gates: no_horizontal_overflow on the 390px mobile home (the tab row must wrap, not pin to a fixed/narrow desktop width that overflows); visual_regression on the browser component crops at desktop_work_grid + mobile_work_grid (on-brand dark surface + lavender accent with a legible active tab and a clean reflowing grid, not an overlapping clipped grid with a dark-on-dark tab); cross-page dom_assertions that the browser title "Selected experiments" rides both case-study routes as well as home; and interaction_assertions that clicking the Post-processing tab re-filters the grid and updates the count to "7 of 18 experiments" (a snapshotted grid+count that never re-derives fails this). The baseline is the original layout defect (tab row pinned to a fixed 640px non-wrapping width, browser present on home only) which fails overflow + visual + cross-page but passes interaction; the known-bad "smart wrong" browser keeps a narrow non-wrapping tab row, breaks the grid into a single overflowing row of fixed-width tiles pulled together with a negative margin so the cards overlap and clip, renders a dark-on-dark illegible active tab, is home-only, and snapshots its grid and count at mount so the tab click succeeds but the terminal result stays stale — failing all four gates. INFRA fixes applied identically to all three legs (not part of the graded change): the offline-determinism typekit stylesheet is dropped from the head, and the unified experiment dataset (lib/experiments.ts) is shared across legs. The local motion assets (good-time.mp4, reflective-cube.mp4, monalisa.mp4, and the wider archive) are the design assets reused as-is.
